items.question: Which model does AMORA use by default?
items.answer: Reef, the free preset: free cloud models through your own free OpenRouter account. Free tiers have small daily quotas, so Reef suits small tasks, and the dashboard shows what's left and warns you before a task is likely to run out. A worker with no free model that meets its requirements is marked as unavailable in free mode rather than given one that doesn't.

items.question: What are Reef, Tide, and Abyss?
items.answer: Presets: a model picked for every worker in one go, so you don't fill 66 slots by hand. Reef is free models only. Tide puts strong low-cost models everywhere and mid-tier ones on the Planner and gatekeepers. Abyss uses frontier models only where they change the outcome. They run on your own gateway account and aren't subscriptions. Every assignment is labelled Verified, Experimental, Unverified, or Rejected.

items.question: Do I have to pay?
items.answer: AMORA is free, and so is the Reef preset as long as you stay inside your gateway's free quota. Beyond that you pay your providers for the tokens your workers use. You set a spending limit per task and per day, and the Costs page shows what each successful task cost. Those figures come from gateway telemetry, so some of them are estimates, and the page says which.

items.question: Do I need Telegram?
items.answer: No. The dashboard does everything. If you want approvals on your phone, connect a Telegram bot in Settings. It gets short summaries and approval buttons, never your keys. Discord is the next adapter on the list.

items.question: Can I use local models?
items.answer: Yes, through Ollama. A local model is probed like any other, and it can only be assigned to workers whose requirements it meets.

items.question: Is my data used for training?
items.answer: AMORA runs on your machine and only sends prompts to the providers you connect, so their terms decide. If you pick a free-tier model, the dashboard warns you that prompts may be used for training. With OpenRouter, data collection is switched off by default.

items.question: How do I change the model for one worker?
items.answer: Assign a different model from the Models page in the dashboard. AMORA checks it against the worker's requirements and refuses it with a clear reason if anything is missing. Give the Slice / Markup Engineer a text-only model, for example, and it gets rejected, because that role needs vision.

items.question: What happens when a worker keeps failing?
items.answer: Each task gets three attempts. After the third, work stops and the decision comes to you. The worker's Interactions tab lists every handoff it sent or received, with the failed ones a click away.

items.question: How is this different from prompt collections like agency-agents?
items.answer: A prompt collection gives you role descriptions to paste into a single model. AMORA runs the work itself: workers execute tasks, pass results to each other through typed contracts, and have to clear quality gates written in code. Each worker also runs on its own model instead of everyone sharing one.
